QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_8

question.text: The Prime Brokerage (PB) Agreement with the Investment Manager of Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III AIF) is being finalised. Which of the following is NOT typically a governance/operational-DD check performed by the manager on the PB arrangement?

answer.text: Rehypothecation limits and segregation of client assets
Margin methodology (SPAN, portfolio margin, TIMS) and intraday margin-call escalation
Asset custody chain-of-title and bankruptcy-remoteness in the PB's home jurisdiction
Allocation of Cat I/II co-investment PE deal-by-deal voting rights

explanation.text: The Logic: Operational due diligence on a prime broker typically covers asset-handling and risk-management terms specific to that relationship: rehypothecation limits and client-asset segregation, margin methodology (SPAN, portfolio margin, TIMS) and intraday margin-call escalation, and custody chain-of-title and bankruptcy-remoteness in the PB's jurisdiction. Deal-by-deal voting allocation belongs to Category I/II PE investment-committee mechanics, not Category III prime-brokerage governance. The Trap: The first three options are canonical PB-DD checks. Option D mixes a PE-fund governance mechanic into an unrelated PB context, which is the giveaway. Note: The specific PB due-diligence items above — rehypothecation, bankruptcy-remoteness, margin-methodology DD, and sub-custody side-letter mechanics — are not explicitly set out in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which mention prime brokers within governance/service-provider context and discuss Category III leverage and derivatives. The framing reflects general industry/regulatory practice for PB operational due diligence.
